content:

Cash Home Buyers in Illinois
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Inherited, behind on payments, tenants, repairs: we buy it as-is
  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs

Selling in Cook County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Cook County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Illinois statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

The Cook County recorder of deeds records Illinois deeds and mortgages. This guide lists what we confirmed on official pages.

Who records deeds in Cook County

  • Cook County Clerk - Recordings Division records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Recording fees: Deeds, Leases, Mortgages/Releases, Easements, Miscellaneous (Doc Classes 1-5) $107; Irregular docs class fee + $88; Transfer on Death Instrument $59; Mechanic's lien $64; Plats $152; recording by mail with return $5 per doc. Fees include GIS, document storage, RHSP and non-gov filer fees.
  • Copies: certified paper $55; certified digital PDF $65; non-certified paper $27.50; non-certified download $5; online card payments carry 2.10% fee.
  • Recordings office hours 9am-5pm, last customer 4:45pm; appointments bookable online.

Recording and transfer tax

  • Quitclaim deed may be in substance the statutory form ('convey and quit claim ... all interest'); form should have a 3.5 x 3.5 inch blank space for recorder (failure does not affect validity); conveys grantor's then-existing legal/equitable rights but not after-acquired title unless words added; recording of a quitclaim solely to reflect a legal name change (same grantor/grantee) is exempt from recording fees (P.A. 104-40, eff. 1-1-26). (765 ILCS 5/10; source)
  • Transfer declaration (PTAX-203) must accompany a deed presented for recordation (or be presented within 3 business days of transfer, whichever earlier), signed by at least one seller and one buyer or agents; deed not accepted for recordation without it except as 31-45 provides. (35 ILCS 200/31-25; source)

Fees

County recording fees change, so we do not quote a total. Check the recorder's current fee schedule before you file.

Selling in Cook County?
We buy Cook County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • Cook Treasurer late-penalty rate (statutory 1.5%/month) not seen on opened page
  • Cook e-recording and PTAX-203/transfer declaration not seen on opened Clerk pages
  • Cook tax rate/millage not retrieved

How to sell a house in Cook County

  1. Find out what the title company needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded deed or the probate paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in Illinois.

Cook County recorder of deeds FAQ

Where do I record a deed in Cook County?

At the county recorder of deeds. Confirm submission rules on the county page.

Do I owe realty transfer tax?

Realty transfer tax can apply to deeds. The Department of Revenue lists the exemptions.
